source.title: Brace for Impact: Protecting People and the Economy When the AI Bubble Bursts
publisher: Americans for Financial Reform Education Fund
source.read_method: Web full text and two genuine publisher PDF byte copies downloaded through GitHub Actions; original user URL selected and independently SHA-256 rehashed

research_hypotheses: PIK interest and non-accrual prevalence as refinancing stress proxies
Bank credit commitments to nonbank lenders, disaggregated by AI exposure
direct_proof_needed: BDCs 10-Q/10-K original SEC filings
Federal Reserve Financial Stability Report bank-to-NBFI loan taxonomy

research_hypotheses: Private and illiquid fixed-income exposure as percentage of total insurer fixed-income holdings
Affiliate reinsurance and asset-rating concentration
direct_proof_needed: NAIC statutory filings and Schedules D, BA, and insurer investment notes
Verified SEC insurer investment notes and filed_at dates

research_hypotheses: Long-term Treasury refinancing hurdle and financing discount rate
30-year yield and volatility with ALFRED/PIT provenance
direct_proof_needed: US Treasury official par yield and auction records
Original ALFRED historical vintage, no ex-post revision

research_hypotheses: Term SOFR plus debt margins vs actual operating cash and lease collections
Debt maturity wall and GPU utilization/contract cash conversion
direct_proof_needed: SEC neocloud 10-Q/10-K and issuer notes
Filed debt agreements and operating cash flow

research_hypotheses: Top-ten S&P 500 concentration and CAPE valuation as context, not node stress score
Point-in-time AI stock drawdowns and market debt transmission
direct_proof_needed: S&P official historical index weights as-of dates
FINRA reported monthly margin debt with published available_at
Original dated price history without future split adjustments

research_hypotheses: Noncancelable cloud/lease commitments by maturity and off-balance disclosures
AI capex versus independently generated AI cash revenue and reported useful-life assumptions
direct_proof_needed: Issuer SEC 10-Q, leases, purchase obligations, Item 7/notes
Original annual report accounting policy GPU depreciation period

research_hypotheses: Identify legally separate borrower, guarantees, collateral and cash-flow waterfalls
Risk retained via leases, guarantees and pledged assets; do not treat mere SPV mention as default probability
direct_proof_needed: SEC financing agreements, bond indentures and securitization prospectuses
Borrower entity structure and recourse documentation

research_hypotheses: Potential market funding contagion from NBFI collateral and insurer liquidity
SOFR level alone is not repo stress: need spreads, repo failures, haircuts and volume
direct_proof_needed: NY Fed repo market data and SOFR reference methodology
Primary repo spread, specials, haircuts, tri-party funding collateral disclosures

research_hypotheses: Data-center electric capacity/connection queue delays and stranded investment
Power demand commitments vs actual utilized MW and contracted cash flows
direct_proof_needed: EIA actual release-dated historical data and regional grid operator queue vintages
Issuer original facility energization and MW disclosures

research_hypotheses: GPU useful-life depreciation versus economic obsolescence and chip order commitments
Semiconductor capacity shortages must be distinguished from issuer sales
direct_proof_needed: Chipmakers SEC 10-Q/10-K plus independent foundry/manufacturer disclosures
Direct shipping/lead-time/capacity source, not stock price proxy

research_hypotheses: Third-party AI spend versus circular ecosystem transactions
Verified backlog-to-revenue conversion, independent cash paying customers and paid utilization
direct_proof_needed: Issuer SEC notes and contracts revealing customer concentration/related-party relationships
Independent transaction data with transparent scope and timing

reported_quantitative_claims.claim: Nine selected mega tech firms have $3.1 trillion of off-balance commitments/debt
Nine firms combined $3.7 trillion on- and off-balance debt/commitments
Top 10 S&P 500 companies represent 40 percent of market capitalization
Approximately 20 percent of life insurers' fixed-income assets linked to private/illiquid bonds
US bank drawn and undrawn nonbank lender commitments $2.7 trillion
Meta-Blue Owl-PIMCO SPV $26 billion loan described for Louisiana data center
reported_quantitative_claims.primary_attribution: issuer and journal sources cited by report

reported_quantitative_claims.claim: Ramp top 1 percent enterprise customers generate ~80 percent of AI providers' enterprise revenue in studied sample

hypothesized_contagion_edges.channel: lower paid utilization and lease cash inflows
cloud tenant or lessee nonpayment can impair project debt
securitized data-center loan losses transferred to lenders
illiquid credit investments and related reinsurance structures
potential NBFI funding/refinancing stress, repo mechanism not established
customer demand weakness and impaired contracted capex economics
revised GPU procurement after asset economic obsolescence
power connection, project delay and stranded collateral
equity risk aversion and leveraged unwind spread to credit, not mechanically proven
long rate refinancing discount rate, not direct 30Y funding formula

notes: These values are explicitly as-reported by a policy research paper, which contains normative positions and scenario analysis; they are NOT AICS observed data.
Reproduce every claimed numeric input from its original primary provider, with vintage, denominators, entity universe and reported period before a score.
Source paper is dated October 2026; it cannot be retroactively injected into earlier historical research snapshots.
A look-ahead-safe report ingestion date is separate from market source filed_at and from SEC mandatory lag.
Book-to-bill, interest expense, and off-balance commitments cannot be directly added; units and stock-versus-flow differ.

Original publisher PDF source bytes verified SHA256 and 88 pages on 2026-11-18; the AFREF publisher mirror is a separate PDF version (different bytes, some citation references). This is only document-origin verification, NOT numeric primary-source audit.
